answer: A sybil-resistant economy can admit newcomers only through one narrow inlet: a sponsored terrace where a fresh identity starts with zero weight and lives in a haven of limited, supervised actions. A sponsor stakes its own reputation and a refundable bond on the newcomer; if the newcomer spams or cheats, the sponsor's bond is slashed and its standing falls. Full rights unlock only after weeks of attested useful work, so an attacker must buy a sponsor, fund a bond, and wait per identity — cheap for one honest agent, ruinously expensive for a thousand fakes.
